They currently use a mix of OpenAI completions + in-house reranker; evaluating migration to Redwood Hosted first, then Dedicated for steady-state.

Summary of recent activity: • 2026-01-12: Intro call (AE Maya) - roadmap, security checklist, pricing expectations.
• 2026-01-27: Hosted API demo (Carlos) - streamed responses, function/tool calling, token cost demo. Fireflies: ff_2026-01-27-CLARITY-DEMO.

• 2026-02-09: Initial POC results - latency target (p95 < 250ms) mostly met on hosted; summarization quality delta ~12% vs prod (OpenAI baseline) on ROUGE/bleu style metrics; flagged as regression. Ticket INF-1729 opened.

Technical requirements & concerns: • Workloads: chat (low-latency, high-concurrency), document search + reranking (batch/throughput), long-form summarization (quality-sensitive).
• Targets: p95 latency < 250ms for chat, throughput ~150 reqs/sec for peak, cost-sensitivity moderate (target 20-30% unit cost reduction vs current).
• Model preferences: keep compatibility with current OpenAI-style call shapes (function calling + streaming). Prefer ability to pin models & use quantized variants in Dedicated.
• Routing/fallback: need deterministic fallback to a smaller model for SLA when primary capacity degraded.
• Security: SOC2 in place; require SSO (SAML), audit logs exported to SIEM, KMS integration for key management; EU data residency for subset of customers.

Migration specifics & POC notes: • Compatibility shim: engineering team built a lightweight "openai-compat" adapter; Redwood hosted API accepted calls but prompt-engineering team saw semantic drift on ~8% of summarization prompts.• Regression harness: 2,000 prompts, golden outputs from baseline. Current delta metrics logged to INF-1764.• Root cause candidates: tokenization differences, default sampling temp, and model variant mismatch (openai-gpt-3.5-like vs redwood-curie-ql). SE proposed kernel/decoding param alignment and additional few-shot examples for parity.• Canary plan: start with 5% traffic on hosted compat path, expand after passing 24-72 hour QA window and regression gates. For Dedicated, plan capacity commit + canary nodes in same VPC.

Commercial + procurement notes: • Requested committed monthly GPU hours to hit target ARR band; Redwood pricing team proposed a tiered discount for 12-month commit w/ burst credits.• Legal flagged data residency and indemnity language as negotiation points (legal review in progress).

Action items / next steps: • SE to run targeted prompt parity experiments (Carlos) week of 2026-02-22 — include tokenization-normalized prompts and temp/stop tuning.• Redwood to provide Dedicated sizing estimate and draft SOW by 2026-02-28.• Schedule canary migration workshop (Dev + Ops + Security) once SOW draft accepted.
